name: Azure Bicep
summary: Azure Bicep is a declarative language for deploying Azure resources. The what-if operation lists what a deployment would create, change or delete before it runs, and Azure keeps the deployment state, so the user does not manage a state file. Microsoft's Bicep page says the language is free and open source.

facts.text: The Bicep overview says Bicep uses declarative syntax, and that a Bicep file defines the infrastructure to deploy to Azure.
The overview says the what-if operation shows which resources to create, update or delete, and which properties to change, before the Bicep file is deployed.
The overview says Azure stores all states, so users have no state files to manage.
The overview says Bicep is free and open source, and that Microsoft Support supports it.

plans.name: Bicep
plans.notes: Free and open source according to the Bicep overview. Azure resources deployed with Bicep are not covered by this price.
